description: Temporal authority: governs_from is DERIVED from anchors, never stored. v0 left the epoch-0 boundary T0 undefined, so implementations supplied it from local state — making it verdict-bearing without being commitment-bearing. These vectors pin the derivation and, crucially, pin that no stored value may reach a verdict. Values are taken from a live deployment (agent 8 of registry 0x8b5af3a5...c3) so they can be cross-checked against published leaves and on-chain anchor timestamps rather than trusted.

rules.R2: key_epoch n>0 -> governs_from = anchored_at of the EARLIEST anchored batch containing the binding's cc
rules.R3: key_epoch n>0 with no containing anchor -> no governs_from, never in force
rules.R4: among bindings with governs_from <= artifact anchor_time and not revoked at/before it, greatest governs_from wins
rules.R5: submitted_at MUST NOT affect any verdict

anchors.note: SYNTHETIC. A later batch re-containing the same still-current leaf — the ordinary case, since every batch includes each agent's current binding. Present solely to pin that re-anchoring does NOT move the boundary forward (R2 says earliest).

bindings.name: e0
bindings.why: R1. The baseline key is the agent's key from creation; there is no honest moment before which it did not govern. Note it is ALSO in anchor 1 at 1785436450 — a conforming implementation must return 0 here, not that anchor time. Deriving epoch 0 from its anchor is precisely the defect this version fixes.

bindings.name: e1
bindings.why: R2. First contained in anchor 2. Note submitted_at is 1435s EARLIER — that gap is the live divergence this version exists to close, and an implementation reading submitted_at would answer 1786548015.

bindings.name: e2-unanchored
bindings.why: R3. Accepted by an implementation but contained in no anchored batch. It has no temporal authority at all — a binding that cannot be proven cannot govern.

cases.name: baseline-governs-from-zero
cases.why: An artifact predating EVERY anchor still resolves to the baseline key. Under a v0 implementation that derived the boundary from the epoch-0 anchor, this returned no_in_force_binding — the live bug that stranded 26 of 26 companions when their agents rotated.

cases.name: successor-governs-from-anchor
cases.why: After the successor is anchored, it governs — and the boundary is the anchor time, not the submission time.

cases.name: pre-anchor-window-resolves-to-predecessor
cases.why: THE v0/v1 DIVERGENCE, made explicit. 1786548500 sits after e1 was submitted (1786548015) but before it was anchored (1786549450). v0 resolved this to e1; v1 resolves it to e0, because during that window the successor was not provable and the predecessor was. Any implementation still reading a stored boundary answers e1 here and fails this case.

cases.name: unanchored-successor-never-in-force
cases.why: Fails closed. e2-unanchored has a later submitted_at than e1 and would win under any submission-ordered rule, but it is in no anchor, so it has no authority and e1 still governs. An implementation that ranked by submitted_at returns e2 here.

cases.name: submitted-at-is-not-verdict-bearing
cases.why: The load-bearing one. submitted_at is moved far into the past — a change that flips the verdict under v0 — and the answer must not move. This tests the SHAPE of the dependency, not its value: a suite that only checks implementations agree can never find a field they all read the same wrong way.

cases.name: earliest-not-latest-containing-anchor
cases.why: e1's leaf is in anchors 2 AND 3 — the ordinary case, since each batch re-includes every current binding. The boundary is anchor 2's time. An implementation taking the latest containing anchor would put governs_from at 1786600000, find it later than this artifact, and wrongly report no key in force.

cases.name: baseline-submitted-at-is-not-verdict-bearing
cases.why: Added after a negative control exposed a hole in this very suite. The other R5 case mutates e1, but e0's submitted_at is 0 — which COINCIDES with R1's answer — so an implementation that wrongly returned submitted_at for the baseline still passed every value-based case. Here e0's submitted_at is moved to 1786000000, later than the artifact, so reading it yields no_in_force_binding while R1 yields e0. Two fields agreeing on one dataset is not the same as one of them being unread.
